Subject: Data use and BAA questions for Redwood Inference

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the routing and residency controls you showed. As we evaluate Redwood for a pilot, InfoSec has a few gate items we need before we can move to procurement: 

- A copy of your current BAA or a redline against our WellCare DPA template (attached)
- SOC 2 Type II (redacted report is fine under NDA)
- Up-to-date subprocessor inventory with contract-level controls and locations
- Confirmation of encryption (TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest) and KMS options (customer-managed ok?)
- Clarification on EU->US transfer mechanisms (SCCs, adequacy reliance, or EU-only private deployments)

Can you indicate a timeline for these items and whether Redwood can sign our DPA language around BAA scoping? We plan to start a small pilot with de-identified PHI next quarter but need the compliance answers to proceed.

Attaching: WellCare_DPA_Template.docx

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Chen
Senior Manager, Vendor Risk 
WellCare Health

Next steps I propose:
1) I
will upload a preliminary BAA redline (attached) for your legal review by EOD Jan 11.

If InfoSec prefers stronger residency guarantees, Redwood offers a Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) or Dedicated capacity in aws-us-west-2 to isolate data. Happy to schedule a short technical call with our platform security lead.

Proposed timing: redline by Jan 11, evidence package by Jan 14, call week of Jan 18.

Best,

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Date: 2027-01-09T11:45:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Data use and BAA questions for Redwood Inference — WellCare

Thanks for the ping — reviewed the WellCare template and Kimberly's draft. High level:

1) BAA scope: we should accept standard HIPAA business associate language but push back on any excessive indemnity/penalty clauses. We can accept WellCare's security measures section with a few clarifying annotations (see comments in attached).

2) SOC2: provide redacted report under NDAs. We have an NDA template if they need one; otherwise ask them to upload to their vendor portal and we'll complete the attestation.

3) Subprocessors: we can provide the CSV export (attached). For a small number of infra partners we can provide signed attestations; otherwise we provide contract summaries and locations.

4) EU transfers: recommend proposing SCCs + a technical option of EU-only private deployment if they need strict residency. SCCs will cover most enterprise buyers, but some European subsidiaries ask for EU-only hosting.

5) KMS/customer-managed keys: OK for Dedicated and Private; Hosted can support customer-managed keys for an additional contractual control (bring-your-own-key via our KMS integration).

6) Timeline: Kimberly's proposed timeline is fine. I'll prepare legal redline responses and a short "compliance packet" (SOC2, subprocessors CSV, encryption architecture sketch).

Attaching: redwood_subprocessors_2026-12.csv

-Aditya
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
